primitives.name: Tiered Entitlement Law
primitives.verbatim_quote: No price/product creation here — only the entitlement **law** between existing products and API surfaces.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T': 'subscription tier {FREE, FANTASY, PRO, ELITE}', 'P': 'Stripe product ID {prod_...}', 'S': 'API surface set {public_api, pro_api, elite_api}'}
primitives.assumptions: Each tier maps uniquely to a set of API surfaces; no dynamic pricing logic exists.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When T = FREE, S = ∅; when T = FANTASY, S = {public_api}; when T = PRO, S = {public_api, pro_api}; when T = ELITE, S = {public_api, pro_api, elite_api}.

layer2.mapping: Entitlement law is an isomorphism between subscription tiers and API surface sets, defined by Stripe product identifiers.
layer2.telemetry: Access logs verify adherence to tiered surface mappings.

primitives.name: API Surface Resolver
primitives.verbatim_quote: Production path: resolve tier from subscription via `tierForPriceId` → pass into handlers.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p': 'price ID (Stripe)', 't': 'resolved tier ∈ {FREE, FANTASY, PRO, ELITE}', 'h': 'handler function'}
primitives.assumptions: Subscription data is consistent with Stripe product catalog; handler receives resolved tier.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs if `tierForPriceId(p)` returns undefined or malformed tier.

layer2.mapping: Resolver kernel derives tier from price ID using internal lookup table; kernel is derived from Stripe product metadata.
layer2.telemetry: Handler invocation logs confirm correct tier resolution.

primitives.name: Query Parameter Tier Filter
primitives.verbatim_quote: Query param `tier=` on `/metrics` and `/metrics/:id` (until session-auth wires real entitlements).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'q': "query parameter string 'tier='", 't_q': 'tier from query param', 't_r': 'resolved tier from auth'}
primitives.assumptions: Session authentication not yet wired; fallback to query param is temporary.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If t_q ≠ t_r, access denied with 403 error.

layer2.mapping: Filter kernel compares query-tier against resolved-tier; rejects mismatched inputs.
layer2.telemetry: HTTP 403 responses validate enforcement of tier consistency.

Failure modes include invalid price IDs, mismatched query parameters, and unauthorized access attempts.
